description: A macro of another module that calls M.seven() while M's body expands it stalls: the compile-time run M's walk waits on needs ModuleInterface(M) (remote call) or FunctionDefined(M.f) (local), which only M's walk produces. The stall frontier words it as unrelated failures: 'module `M` is not defined', 'function `main/0` is not defined', 'module `Helper` does not export `make/0`'. Elixir: '** (UndefinedFunctionError) function M.seven/0 is undefined (function not available) ... expanding macro: Helper.make/0'. Probe: scratchpad s144/p/back.fz (Helper.make calls M.seven; M imports Helper, defines seven/0, then calls make()). Done when: the stall frontier recognises a definition-time run that waits on the module whose walk waits on it, and reports one diagnostic naming the called function and that the module is still being defined, on interp/run/build; refusal fixture for the macro case.
title: Code that runs while a module is being defined and calls into it is refused in Elixir's words
